W3 (cost lens), after E010. The tip is E010: Muon, Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 at 40/30/30%, 9.5 epochs, batch 2000, last group narrowed to 512. It scores 6.64 s at 0.7548, a margin of only 0.18 pp over the 0.753 bar and below my ~0.756 safety bar for the 40-seed judgment.

Measured prices:
- Compile plus fused SGD: −14% time (E003/E004). Recompile leaks cost about +3 s.
- EMA: +0.97 pp, nearly free (E005).
- Muon: +0.66 pp for +4% time (E006).
- Resizing (E007): −22% time for −0.59 pp, about 3.5 s per pp.
- Epochs 9.5 vs 9 (E008): 0.35 s for 0.18 pp, about 2 s per pp.
- Width 576→512 (E010): −0.34 s (−4.8%) for −0.25 pp, about 1.4 s per pp. That was the cheapest accuracy-for-time trade so far, but it consumed most of the margin.
- LR decay to 0 on top of EMA: noise (E009). EMA already fills the low-LR role.

Budget model: time ≈ F + V × pixel fraction. F (fixed: H2D, pad, whitening, Lookahead setup) is about 0.5-0.8 s. V ≈ 7.5-8 s full-res-equivalent at 9.5 epochs and width 512. The current pixel fraction is 0.755. Small resolutions use the GPU less efficiently, so I discount the saving below 24 px by about 30%. I expect accuracy loss from resizing to grow super-linearly as the 32-px tail shrinks.

Systems: each step is about 25 ms of GPU-saturated work. Launch and Python overhead is probably ≤3%, so CUDA graphs have little to gain and carry real risk. Fused SGD uses Python-float LRs, Muon is compiled separately, and the Lookahead step is Python. Those parts stay outside the graph or force static-buffer copies. Remaining systems levers are small: the augment mask loop (25 masked copies per epoch) and per-epoch interpolate plus permute copies.

Strategy implication: with no margin left, every pure time cut must be paid for by a near-free accuracy gain first. Candidates are LS/wd/LR retunes, BN recalibration after EMA, and better augmentation. Otherwise the tip has to buy margin back with epochs at about 2 s per pp. The best trades are those under 2 s per pp. Width was one; aggressive resizing could be another (estimated ~1.5 s per pp), but only once margin exists.

Noise:
- Compiled runs are deterministic per seed. E003 and E004 gave identical accuracy.
- Per-seed std is about 0.2-0.35 pp, so the 3-seed SE is about 0.15-0.2 pp. Time noise is about 1-2%.
- My misses were underestimating accuracy gains from known-good airbench components (EMA, Muon, resizing) and overestimating times early on.

Unsure about:
- the offset between seeds 0-2 and the 40-seed mean (it matters a lot at 0.18 pp of margin);
- whether ≤20 px is super-linearly harmful;
- whether LS 0.2 vs 0.3 or a wd retune is free accuracy;
- the true launch-overhead fraction under the 4-CPU pin.

forecasts.reason: Pixel fraction falls from 0.755 to 0.639. That saves about 0.6 s after discounting for poor GPU use at 20 px, but losing 0.4-0.6 pp pushes the tip, which has only 0.18 pp of margin, below 0.753. The trade (about 1.5 s per pp) is cheaper than cutting epochs, yet the run comes out infeasible.
The recipe is unchanged, so time matches the tip. The held-out mean should fall within 0.3 pp of seeds 0-2, with per-seed std around 0.2-0.35 pp.

Steps are about 25 ms and GPU-bound, so launch overhead is only a few percent. The optimizer and Lookahead stay partly outside the graph and static-input copies add cost, so a ≥3% cut is unlikely and the leak/breakage risk is real.

cruxes: What is the offset between the seeds 0-2 mean and a 10+-seed mean for the E010 tip? With only 0.18 pp of margin, this decides whether the tip must buy back accuracy before any further time cut.

Is there a near-free accuracy gain (LS 0.2, a wd/LR retune, BN recalibration after EMA) worth ≥0.3 pp, which could then be spent on aggressive resizing at about 1.5 s per pp or on epochs at about 2 s per pp?
Does accuracy loss from resizing grow super-linearly below 24 px or with a 32-px tail under 30%? That sets whether I011-style schedules beat epoch cuts per pp.
